questions.text: An architect installs accessible ramps and an accessible toilet to comply with BP 344. The building owner asks whether this investment yields any tax benefit. Which answer correctly evaluates the situation?

options.text: No tax benefit applies to accessibility improvements since these are mandatory code compliance costs, which are not incentivized
The owner may claim up to 50% additional deduction on direct accessibility improvement costs under RA 7277 incentives
The owner receives a 25% tax credit (not deduction) on accessibility improvement costs under RA 10754, which can be applied to future tax liabilities
The owner receives full exemption from real property tax on floors that contain accessible features, significantly reducing tax obligations

questions.rationale: Up to 50% additional deduction on direct accessibility improvement costs is available under RA 7277 incentive provisions and BIR guidance. Beyond normal depreciation, the Philippine law framework — specifically RA 7277 as amended and BIR implementing rules — allows businesses to claim an additional deduction of up to 50% of the direct costs of installing accessibility improvements such as ramps, lifts, and accessible toilets that comply with BP 344. This is distinct from the 25% wage deduction (which applies only to PWD employee salaries). The improvement deduction effectively subsidizes BP 344 compliance by reducing taxable income, making accessibility economically less burdensome.
questions.explanation: Up to 50% additional deduction on direct accessibility improvement costs effectively subsidizes BP 344 compliance.
questions.code_citation: RA 7277 as amended; BIR guidance on accessibility improvements

questions.text: What is the source-safe interpretation of a 1500 mm sidewalk or walkway requirement?

questions.rationale: BP 344 supports sidewalk and walkway widths as accessibility-route dimensions, not benefit-law provisions.
questions.explanation: RA 10754 is the specific law that added the 12% VAT exemption alongside the 20% discount for PWDs.

questions.text: What should an architect do with PWD discount, VAT, employment quota, tax incentive, or penalty claims when the local RA/BIR source packet is unavailable?

options.text: Use BP 344 dimensions as proof of those benefits
Defer or narrow the item until the local law packet is acquired

questions.rationale: Privilege-law claims require their own verified local source packet; the safe batch action is to defer those claims or narrow to locally supported accessibility design.
questions.explanation: The 1% government employment quota comes from RA 10524 — a common misattribution to RA 9442 Section 35 is a documented exam trap.

questions.text: A private company with 120 employees wants to understand its PWD employment obligations. Under the Philippine law framework, which statement correctly describes the company's obligation?

options.text: It must reserve exactly 1% of positions for PWDs as an absolute legal mandate under RA 10524
It is encouraged to reserve at least 1% of positions for PWDs under RA 10524 and anti-discrimination provisions
It has no legal obligation to hire PWDs since employment quotas apply only to government agencies
It must reserve 5% of positions for PWDs since it is a large private employer with over 100 employees

questions.rationale: Private companies with 100+ employees are encouraged (not strictly mandated) to reserve 1% of positions for PWDs. The 1% employment quota is a firm absolute mandate for government agencies and corporations under RA 10524. For private companies with 100 or more employees, the 1% reservation is encouraged and backed by anti-discrimination provisions, but the framing in RA 10524 and RA 7277 amendments is less absolute for the private sector than for the public sector. Failure to make good-faith efforts can trigger anti-discrimination enforcement, but the private sector framing is 'encouraged' rather than a hard criminal mandate.
questions.explanation: Government: 1% is an absolute mandate. Private (100+ employees): 1% is encouraged with anti-discrimination backing.
